mission_07: Congratulations on implementing a streaming ASR system! You now understand the architectural choices required for real-time speech recognition. The chunked processing approach balances latency and accuracy: smaller chunks reduce latency but provide less context for recognition, while larger chunks improve accuracy at the cost of higher latency. The overlap between chunks preserves temporal context at boundaries, preventing information loss where words span chunk edges. The stateful encoder passes hidden representations between chunks, enabling the model to build coherent understanding across the entire audio stream rather than treating each chunk independently. Feature extraction on each chunk must be consistent with the model's training configuration to ensure reliable predictions. The buffer management ensures that all audio is processed, including the final partial chunk. This streaming architecture is the foundation for live captioning, real-time voice assistants, and simultaneous speech translation systems that must produce output as the user speaks.
